Responsabilidades Las responsabilidades se organizan según la matriz de procesos (RACI) del grupo. En cada subproceso se indica si el puesto ejecuta la tarea, la supervisa y aprueba , o ambas. Tesorería y gestión de fondos: Gestionar la tesorería y los fondos del grupo, administrando bancos y sociedades en los distintos países donde opera. Planificar y monitorear la liquidez, las transferencias entre entidades y la exposición a distintas monedas. Facturación: Supervisar y aprobar la facturación que ejecuta el analista del área, en todos los mercados. Cobranzas — ejecuta y aprueba: Gestionar directamente las cobranzas de todas las compañías y mercados, incluyendo seguimiento de deudores y antigüedad de saldos. Pagos — ejecuta: Programar y ejecutar los pagos a proveedores y terceros de todas las entidades. Contabilidad e impuestos Sueldos y nómina — supervisa (Argentina) y ejecuta (exterior) Control de gestión Procesos y control interno Perfil buscado • Contador/a Público/a o Licenciado/a en Administración. Posgrado en finanzas o control de gestión, deseable. • Al menos 8 años de experiencia en administración y finanzas, de los cuales 3 o más en una posición de liderazgo del área. • Experiencia en grupos con varias sociedades y operación multipaís y multimoneda (Argentina y Estados Unidos, idealmente otros países de LATAM). • Manejo de tesorería con bancos locales e internacionales. • Conocimiento de liquidación de sueldos en Argentina y de esquemas de pago a contractors en el exterior. • Experiencia en empresas de servicios (agencias, IT, staffing), deseable. • Excel avanzado y armado de reportes de gestión (P&L, cash flow, presupuesto). • Manejo de ERP y sistemas de gestión contable. • Normativa impositiva argentina; nociones de fiscalidad de Estados Unidos (LLC, contractors). • Inglés intermedio-avanzado. • Perfil flexible, capaz de adaptarse a liderar un área con distintas unidades de negocios y en distintos países • Autonomía y capacidad de trabajar de forma remota con alto nivel de responsabilidad. • Habilidad para gestionar la relación con un CEO, involucrado y exigente, con criterio propio y comunicación clara y firme. • Orientación a ordenar: definir procesos, documentarlos y lograr que se cumplan. • Liderazgo de equipos pequeños y capacidad de "hacer y supervisar" a la vez. • Confidencialidad y ética profesional.

review_candidates.title: Content Creator
review_candidates.description: Every Story Shapes How Midland Heart Is Understood. As our Content Creator, you'll play a key role in shaping that understanding. Working across our communities, you'll meet tenants, colleagues and partners, uncovering the stories, issues and successes that best showcase who we are, what we do and the difference we make. Working as part of our External Affairs team, you'll combine creativity with strong editorial judgement to identify the stories that will have the greatest impact. Whether it's a tenant success story, a community initiative or a development milestone, you'll know not only how to tell a compelling story, but where and when to tell it to achieve maximum reach and influence. From photography and video to social media, news stories and campaigns, you'll create content that builds trust, strengthens our reputation, supports our employer brand and helps people better understand Midland Heart. Every piece of content will contribute to a clear, consistent narrative about our organisation and the value we bring to the communities we serve. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include: Creating compelling photography and video content for tenant stories, news, announcements, partnerships, events and corporate milestones. Listening to tenants and colleagues to spot story opportunities and emerging trends, capturing quotes, interviews and written content to use across press, digital and corporate channels. Developing, launching and managing our expanded social media presence, including LinkedIn, alongside content for our app and website. Working with the External Communications Manager to turn PR priorities into content that supports our wider communications objectives. Acting as a custodian of our brand, advising colleagues on tone and quality, and working with designers, suppliers and internal teams to keep standards high. Our ideal candidate? Please upload a copy of your CV alongside a portfolio of your work (instead of a cover letter) in order to be considered for this role. These will demonstrate the following: Hands-on experience in content creation across photography, videography and digital storytelling, including using professional equipment in live or fast-paced environments. Up-to-date knowledge of digital content trends, news and current affairs, with an understanding of how different channels support our objectives. Strong project management skills, with the ability to juggle multiple priorities, work to deadlines and stay within brand guidelines. A sound understanding of GDPR and consent, particularly when filming and photographing tenants and communities. Relevant training or qualifications in media, digital, communications or a related field, and experience working in or closely with communications, PR or corporate affairs teams. Please note: We are unable to consider applications which don't include a portfolio of work in place of a cover letter. Who are Midland Heart? We're one team working together for our tenants. A large, ambitious housing organisation providing people with an affordable place to call home. We value people from all walks of life and strive to create an inclusive environment where you can grow your career and make an impact. We expect a lot from our people, but in return, you'll find a supportive and rewarding workplace where great people thrive. Interested? Please scroll down below for a full Role Profile. Applying is easy - simply register on our candidate portal uploading a CV and a portfolio of your work, which show us that you have what it takes to make a success of the role. We're proud to be a Disability Confident Employer. Please feel free to contact us if you would like to discuss any adjustments you might need in order to be successful in this role.

review_candidates.description: Apply now Job no: 596576 Contract type: Consultant Duty Station: Lome Level: Consultancy Location: Togo Categories: Human Resources L’UNICEF travaille dans plus de 190 pays et territoires pour sauver la vie des enfants, défendre leurs droits et les aider à réaliser leur plein potentiel, de la petite enfance à l’adolescence. À l’UNICEF, nous sommes engagés, passionnés et fiers de ce que nous faisons, aussi longtemps que notre présence est nécessaire. Promouvoir les droits de chaque enfant n’est pas simplement un métier - c’est une vocation. L’UNICEF est un lieu où les carrières se construisent : nous offrons à notre personnel des opportunités variées de développement professionnel et personnel, leur permettant de renforcer leur sentiment d’utilité tout en servant les enfants et les communautés à travers le monde, avec en prime un ensemble attractif de rémunérations et d’avantages. Nous vous invitons à consulter notre site web (website) pour en savoir plus sur les activités et le mandat de l’UNICEF. TERMES DE REFERENCE Sous la supervision de la Représentante et en étroite collaboration avec les sections programmatiques et opérationnelles, le/la consultant(e) fournira un appui technique et méthodologique au bureau dans les domaines de la gestion stratégique des ressources humaines, de la planification des effectifs, du développement organisationnel et de l’alignement des capacités institutionnelles sur les priorités du futur Programme de Coopération. Si vous souhaitez obtenir de plus d’amples informations sur cette consultance, notamment concernant les livrables détaillés et les résultats attendus, veuillez consulter les Termes de Référence complets ici ToR Stratg RH 2028-32.pdf Qualifications minimales requises: (Expérience / connaissances / expertise / compétences requises) Domaines d'education Gestion des Ressources Humaines ; Administration Publique ; Développement Organisationnel ; Management ; Gestion de programmes ; Ou tout autre domaine pertinent. Expérience Professionnelle Au moins dix (10) années d’expérience en gestion des ressources humaines ; Expérience significative dans une organisation internationale, de préférence au sein du système des Nations Unies ; Expérience démontrée en workforce planning, gestion du changement, développement organisationnel et gestion des talents ; Expérience avérée dans l’élaboration ou l’accompagnement de programmes pays, cadres stratégiques ou réformes organisationnelles ; Solides compétences analytiques et rédactionnelles ; Exigences linguistiques Excellente maîtrise du français oral et écrit. Une bonne connaissance de l'anglais constitue un atout. Atouts Souhaitables Avoir participé à l'élaboration d'un CPD, UNSDCF, CCA ou document stratégique similaire. Connaissance des procédures et outils de programmation de l'UNICEF. Pour chaque enfant, vous devez démontrer... Les valeurs fondamentales de l'UNICEF, à savoir la bienveillance, le respect, l'intégrité, la confiance, la responsabilité et la durabilité (CRITAS). Elles sont à la base de tout ce que nous faisons et de la manière dont nous le faisons. Découvrez notre Charte des valeurs : Valeurs de l'UNICEF L'UNICEF est là pour servir les enfants les plus défavorisés du monde et notre personnel doit refléter la diversité de ces enfants. L'UNICEF s'est engagé à inclure tout le monde, indépendamment de la race/l'ethnie, de l'âge, du handicap, de l'identité sexuelle, de l'orientation sexuelle, de la religion, de la nationalité, de l'origine socio-économique ou de toute autre caractéristique personnelle. Nous proposons un large éventail de mesures visant à inclure une main-d'œuvre plus diversifiée, comme le congé parental payé, les heures pour allaitement et des aménagements raisonnables pour les personnes handicapées. L'UNICEF encourage vivement le recours à des modalités de travail flexibles. Selon la Convention des Nations Unies relative aux droits des personnes vivant avec un handicap (UNCRPD), les personnes vivant avec un handicap comprennent celles qui présentent des déficiences physiques, mentales, intellectuelles ou sensorielles durables qui, en interaction avec diverses barrières, peuvent faire obstacle à leur pleine et effective participation à la société sur la base de l'égalité avec les autres. Dans sa politique et sa stratégie d'inclusion des personnes vivant avec un handicap 2022-2030, l'UNICEF s'est engagé à augmenter le nombre d'employés vivant avec un handicap d'ici 2030. À l'UNICEF, nous prévoyons des aménagements raisonnables pour répondre aux besoins de soutien liés au travail des candidats et des employés vivant avec un handicap. L'UNICEF a également mis en place un service d'assistance à l'accessibilité afin de renforcer l'accessibilité physique et numérique. Si vous êtes un candidat vivant avec un handicap et que vous avez besoin d'un soutien en matière d'accessibilité numérique pour remplir le formulaire de candidature en ligne, veuillez soumettre votre demande par le biais du bouton d'accessibilité par courriel sur la page Web des carrières de l'UNICEF Accessibilité | UNICEF. L'UNICEF n'engage pas de candidats mariés à des enfants (personnes de moins de 18 ans). L'UNICEF applique une politique de tolérance zéro à l'égard des comportements incompatibles avec les buts et objectifs des Nations Unies et de l'UNICEF, notamment l'exploitation et les abus sexuels, le harcèlement sexuel, l'abus de pouvoir et la discrimination. L'UNICEF s'engage à promouvoir la protection et la sauvegarde de tous les enfants. Tous les candidats sélectionnés feront l'objet d'une vérification rigoureuse de leurs références et de leurs antécédents et devront adhérer à ces normes et principes. Le contrôle des antécédents comprendra la vérification des titres universitaires et des antécédents professionnels. Les candidats sélectionnés peuvent être amenés à fournir des informations supplémentaires pour la vérification de leurs antécédents, et les candidats vivant avec handicap sélectionnés peuvent être invités à soumettre des documents justificatifs relatifs à leur handicap de manière confidentielle. Les candidat(e)s qualifié(e)s sont invité(e)s à soumettre les documents suivants via le portail de recrutement en ligne (TMS) : Un profil TMS à jour ainsi qu’un curriculum vitae (CV) actualisé Une lettre de motivation Une proposition technique détaillée:  Une méthodologie claire, structurée et détaillée, accompagnée d’un chronogramme précis des activités, à présenter dans un document n’excédant pas cinq (5) pages Une offre financière distincte (uniquement acceptée au format du modèle fourni en pièce jointe) Propos. Par ailleurs, l’UNICEF ne demandera jamais les coordonnées bancaires des candidat(e)s. Tous les postes à l’UNICEF sont publiés publiquement, et seuls les candidat(e)s présélectionné(e)s seront contacté(e)s et convié(e)s à poursuivre le processus de sélection. review_candidates.description: About JFCS Long Beach and Orange County   Founded in 1958, JFCS empowers people to make positive changes through professional mental health care and provides families in crisis with a safety-net of supportive services. JFCS serves a tapestry of clients across  all religious, cultural, and economic backgrounds, and throughout the human life span.   Program Background: Based on the Jewish tradition of “welcoming the stranger,” JFCS provides supportive  resettlement services to refugees and humanitarian parolees to ensure their success, fair treatment and full  integration into American society.   Position Opportunity: JFCS is looking for a compassionate, mission-driven, bilingual individual to join our  Refugee Assistance team as a Bilingual Case Manager – Employment Navigation. You must be fluent in  English as well as Ukrainian and Russian. You will provide case management to eligible Ukrainian immigrants by providing employment assistance, housing assistance, financial literacy tools and cultural  orientation; providing non-legal assistance with preparing applications for re-parole and EAD renewals. You will  help refugees identify career goals, overcome barriers to work, secure appropriate jobs, and maintain  employment. Knowledge of U.S. corporate culture and job search strategies, along with strengths in resume  creation, and employment coaching will be critical to your success.   You will also help develop a pilot workforce development program for Ukrainian refugees interested in careers  in caregiving. This may include supporting clients in meeting California Home Care Aide registration  requirements . This pilot program will then be rolled out to other JFCS immigrant populations. This role bridges  the gap between immigrant job seekers, community organizations, and local employers.  Core Responsibilities  The Bilingual Case Manager-Employment Navigation will:  • Provide case management and employment navigation to refugees and other immigrants. • Help clients explore occupations, understand local labor-market opportunities, identify transferable  skills, and navigate employment programs, job-search resources, and training pathways.  • Help develop a new workforce development pilot program for Ukrainian refugees with a goal to expand  the program to other immigrant populations.  • Assist with resumes, cover letters, job applications, interview preparation, and job-search strategies. Skills/Abilities We’d like you to Have:  • Bachelor’s degree OR at least 2 years of professional experience working as a case manager, social  worker, employment coach, or other position with direct client contact and experience. • Experience working with immigrants, refugees, asylum seekers or other displaced communities. • Knowledge of nonprofit environment and/or social service and employment resources.  Other Benefits  In addition to standard pay, compensation for this position includes:  • Comprehensive, low-cost health/dental care coverage for employees  • Employer 403(b) contributions and life insurance  Time Away from Work  We believe that being able to take time away from work is critical in bringing your best self to work. Time off  benefits for this position include:  • Generous paid vacation time and sick leave  • 13 holidays plus 3 additional personal flex days each year  To apply, please send a cover letter and resume with ‘Bilingual Case Manager-Employment Navigation’  in the subject line, highlighting your interest and qualifications to jobs@jfcslboc.org.  Please, no phone calls. Local candidates only as relocation is not provided. JFCS seeks to recruit, develop, and retain the most talented people and  believes that diversity and inclusion among our teammates is critical to our success in serving our local communities.

It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability. ABOUT WFP The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of extreme weather shocks. At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves. To learn more about WFP, visit our website: https://www.wfp.org and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok. WHY JOIN WFP? WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate. WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment. WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities. A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe. We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement). Overview Of The Role WFP is seeking an Assistant Executive Director, Workplace and Management (United Nations Assistant Secretary-General level) to serve as a core member of its Senior Leadership Team. The incumbent will provide leadership for human resources and staff wellbeing, and across WFP’s enabling functions, including management services, security and technology, ensuring a harmonious and results-driven work environment and that functions are aligned to support effective mandate delivery across global headquarters and country operations. The AED Workplace and Management will play a critical role in strengthening WFP’s organizational effectiveness, operational resilience, and duty of care in a complex and evolving global environment. The incumbent will drive a coherent, accountable and results oriented approach to people, systems, services and security, with a focus on simplifying processes, empowering managers and staff, driving change, improving transparency, and ensuring that WFP’s resources are managed responsibly in support of principled humanitarian action. As a senior leader, the AED will help advance WFP’s contribution to UN reform, including leading efforts to strengthen collaboration across the UN system to ensure that management practices enable agile, cost effective and accountable delivery, including through shared premises and services, where possible. The role requires a leader of the highest integrity and credibility, able to build trust across the organization, engage effectively with Member States, UN partners and governing bodies, and model the values and standards expected of WFP’s senior leadership. Expected Responsibilities As a member of WFP's cohesive Senior Leadership Team, work closely with the Executive Director, Deputy Executive Director and COO, Assistant Executive Directors and other senior leaders to shape and implement policies, strategies, and initiatives that advance WFP's mission and goals. Provide comprehensive strategic direction and guidance across WFP's Workplace and Management Department ensuring that enabling services are coherent, accountable, and responsive to the needs of the organization. Offer strategic leadership in integrating management functions across the organization to ensure effective coordination and alignment. Support WFP’s contribution to UN Reform and related initiatives by championing operational efficiency, mandate alignment, and structural reform, ensuring WFP remains a model of innovation and cost-effectiveness within the UN system. Set the tone for a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement, setting high standards of integrity and ethical behavior for all staff. Promote a positive and inclusive workplace culture that values diversity, equity, and inclusion and fosters an environment of respect and collaboration across all levels of the organization. Oversee WFP’s duty of care and staff wellbeing agenda, including physical and mental health, occupational safety and health, and support to the personnel serving in hardship and high-risk duty stations. Engage and represent WFP in high-level fora (e.g. United Nations, including High Level Committee on Management, Governments, Executive Board, relevant humanitarian and development committees, etc.), asserting the organization’s position and ensuring that WFP interests are at the forefront of discussions and considerations. Promote and set the tone for innovation, efficiency and effectiveness internally and in engagement with other UN agencies and partners Undertake additional responsibilities as required to support WFP’s mission and the Senior Leadership Team. Core Requirements Experience: A minimum of 20 years of progressively responsible experience in senior management, administration or other relevant fields Knowledge & Skills: Strong track record of leadership and strategic management at the international level, preferably in humanitarian or development sectors Proven track record and experience in successfully managing and leading roles with significant breadth and complexity in related fields such as Administration, Security, Human Resources or Facilities Strong leadership and management skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with stakeholders at all levels. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence and persuade at the highest levels. Demonstrated ability in fostering a culture of respect, collaboration, and inclusion, with a strong commitment to diversity and gender equity. Successfully managed a significant budget and operating plan, and a multi-disciplinary team of experts across a variety of job functions. High level of emotional intelligence, with the ability to manage complex and challenging situations with empathy and tact. Impeccable personal and professional integrity, with a firm commitment to the work, objectives, values, and guiding principles of WFP and the United Nations system. Demonstrated experience in leading innovation and promoting operational efficiency in complex environments. Strong networking and relationship-building skills, supported by a well-established network of international stakeholders and partners. Willingness to travel to different locations worldwide, often in challenging and remote environments. LANGUAGES AND EDUCATION Fluency (level C) in English language Working knowledge proficiency of a second official UN language: Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, Spanish, and/or Portuguese (a WFP working language) highly desirable An advanced university degree in Organizational Development, Business Administration, Leadership, Public Administration or related field. TERMS AND CONDITIONS The selected candidate will be employed on a fixed-term contract at the Assistant Secretary General level, with a probationary period of one year. WFP offers an attractive compensation and benefits package, including basic salary, post adjustment, relocation entitlement, travel and shipment allowances, 30 days’ annual leave, as well as expatriate entitlements such as home leave, an education grant for dependent children, and compulsory pension plan and medical insurance. For more details please visit icsc.un.org. All applications should include a cover letter and the curriculum vitae of the candidate in English and must be submitted through the WFP Careers website.
